messages:
soph: Heads-up from Performance review with HighTide  renewal note: they reported p95 drifting to ~300ms during EU mornings and mentioned cost pressure if we don’t show a plan :worried:
miguel: Any idea if this is compute-limited or queuing?
tara: Traces show high queue_depth and frequent KV-cache invalidations on their long-running sessions. They're on a 30B fp16 endpoint, no quantization.
soph: My recommendation: run a two-week "latency shield" canary: 1) deploy a 30B-int8 variant on a dedicated pool for priority routes; 2) add an always-on hosted compact-8b fallback for burst traffic; 3) prefer-dedicated routing weekdays 7-19 CET.
miguel: Canary splits: 4% -> hightide-30b-int8 (dedicated-eu), 6% -> hightide-8b-compact (hosted-fallback). Keep a 5% safety throttle for DB-backed flows.
tara: ML notes: int8 build needs attention-kernel tuning for seq_len up to 2048 and a KV-prefetch policy to reduce miss rate. Also run regen-quality and hallucination checks on their eval corpus.
soph: Can you prepare the eval prompts + quick A/B script? CS wants token-cost delta, regen-fidelity (ROUGE/F1/regression rate), and incidence of truncation/hallucination for the renewal packet.
tara: Draft canary manifest (snippet): ```json
{
  "canary": { "percent": 4 },
  "models": [
    { "name": "hightide-30b-int8", "route": "dedicated-eu" },
    { "name": "hightide-8b-compact", "route": "hosted-fallback" }
  ],
  "timeouts": { "per_request_ms": 2400 },
  "circuit_breaker": { "retries": 1, "failover_on_retry": true }
}
```
miguel: Ops rollout notes: pre-warm KV cache on canary nodes, enable KV-prefetch + sticky-session affinity for priority users, expose queue_depth metric and set alert at >8, set per-route timeout 2.4s, and failover to compact on 1 retry. Also scale min_instances=2 for canary pools.
soph: What's a ballpark cost delta we can present?
tara: Rough estimates: int8 ~30-40% token-cost savings vs fp16 for steady traffic; 8b compact ~60-75% on fallback traffic. Latency: int8 compute may add +10-25ms for short sequences, but overall p95 should fall because of less queuing.
miguel: Also propose a tiny model-mix trial: if regen-f1 drop <1.5pt and hallucination rate stable, bump canary to 12% for 24 hours to gather scaling signals. 
soph: Good idea. CS will want rollback triggers: regen-f1 drop >2.0pt, hallucination increase >0.5%, sustained user flags >1% over 30m. Log prompt_id + eval_id and attach to ticket if flagged.
devops-bot: Reminder: create ticket CS-10024 for HighTide latency-shield canary and attach ML-EVAL-1022.
soph: Thanks team  tagging @miguel @tara. Tara, can you drop the eval suite and a short checklist by EOD? I'll schedule a 25-min handoff with HighTide next Tue to run through tradeoffs and a proposed canary window Thu 6-8am CET.
tara: Will post artifacts and checklist by EOD. Includes regen scripts, automated scoring, and a tiny feedback form for HighTide to flag perceived quality issues during the canary.
soph: This plan should reduce unit cost for HighTide and give a clear measurable path to stabilize p95 before renewal. :thumbsup:
